ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle LMN, with vertex L above, and M and N at the two ends of the base; a circle is inside the triangle and tangent to the three sides, with the center labeled P. Beside the right side LN is marked the length 8 in.. Reasoning: The problem states that triangle LMN is an equilateral triangle, and ⊙P is its incircle, so the radius of the circle is equal to the inradius of an equilateral triangle with side length 8. The formula for the inradius of an equilateral triangle is r = s√3/6. Substituting s = 8 gives r = 8√3/6 = 4√3/3 = 4/√3. The circumference of the circle C = 2πr = 2π(4/√3) = 8π/√3.

raw_record.question_text: $\odot P$ is inscribed in equilateral triangle $LMN$. What is the circumference of $\odot P$?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an equilateral triangle LMN with an inscribed circle centered at P, and note that the side LN is labeled 8 in. From the text, use that the circle is inscribed in the equilateral triangle, so its radius is the inradius of the equilateral triangle. Apply the equilateral-triangle inradius formula r = s\sqrt{3}/6 with s = 8, giving r = 4/\sqrt{3}. Then compute the circumference C = 2\pi r = 8\pi/\sqrt{3}.
